entries.sanskrit:
श्री-गणेशाय नमः । श्री-गोपाल-कृष्णाय नमः ।

तृतीये तु त्रयस्त्रिंशद्-अध्यायैः सर्ग-वर्णनम् ।

ईशेक्षया गुण-क्षोभात् सर्गो ब्रह्माणाद् असम्भवः ॥

तत्र तु प्रथमेऽध्याये बन्धून् हित्वा गतायुषः ।

निर्गतस्योद्धवेनादौ सम्वादः क्षत्तुर् उच्यते ॥

भगवद् ब्रह्म-संप्रोक्तं सङ्क्षेप्त वर्णितं पुरा ।

प्राह भागवतं शेष-प्रोक्तं विस्तरतः पुनः ॥

द्वेधा हि श्रीमद्-भागवत-सम्प्रदाय-प्रवृत्तिः । एकतः सङ्क्षेपतः श्री-नारायण-ब्रह्म-नारदादि-द्वारेण, अन्यतस् तु विस्तरतः शेष-सनत्-कुमार-साङ्ख्यायनादि-द्वारेण । तत्र द्वितीये श्री-नारायण-ब्रह्म-संवादेन सङ्क्षेपतोऽहम् एवासम् इत्य्-आदि चतुः-श्लोक्या श्री-भागवतं निरूपितम् । तद् एव ब्रह्म-नारद-संवादेन दश-लक्षणतया किञ्चिद् विस्तरेणोक्तम् । तद् एव शेषोक्तम् अतिविस्तरतो वक्तुं तृतीयाद्य्-आरम्भः ।

तत्र तृतीये प्रथमं क्षत्तुर् मैत्रेय-सङ्गमश् चतुर्भिर् अध्यायैः, ततोऽष्टभिः स-विसर्गः सर्ग-प्रपञ्चः । ततो विसर्ग-प्रस्तावेन सप्तभिर् वराहावतारः । तत एकेन विसर्ग-समाहारः। तत्-प्रसङ्गेन चतुर्भिः कपिलावतारः। ततो नवभिः कपिलाख्यानम् ।इति त्रयस्त्रिंशताध्यायैस् तृतीय-स्कन्ध-प्रवृत्तिः । तत्र द्वितीय-स्कन्धान्ते---

> परिमाणं च कालस्य कल्प-लक्षण-विग्रहम् । >
> यथा पुरस्ताद् व्याख्यास्ये पाद्मं कल्पम् अथो शृणु ॥\[भा।पु। > २.१०.४७\]

इति प्रतिज्ञातम् अर्थं विस्तरेण निरूपयितुम् इतिहासं प्रस्तौति भगवान् शुकः, एवम् इति द्वाभ्याम् । ऋद्धिमत् सर्व-सम्पद्भिः सम्पूर्णम् ॥१॥
word_for_word: in the Third Canto, through thirty-three chapters
from the agitation of the guṇas by the Lord’s glance
of one whose life had passed
of the one who had departed, first with Uddhava
the dialogue of Vidura is narrated
spoken by Śeṣa, again at length
the transmission of the Śrīmad-Bhāgavata is indeed twofold
through Śrī Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Nārada and others
through Śeṣa, Sanatkumāra, Sāṅkhyāyana and others
through the dialogue of Śrī Nārāyaṇa and Brahmā
through the four verses beginning ‘I alone existed’
through the dialogue of Brahmā and Nārada, in the form of ten characteristics
that same teaching spoken by Śeṣa
to be spoken in great detail, the Third Canto begins
the meeting of Vidura and Maitreya, in four chapters
the creation and secondary creation, the elaboration of creation, in eight
a summary of creation, in one
the incarnation of Kapila, in four
the account of Kapila, in nine
the Third Canto proceeds in thirty-three chapters
hear now about the Pādma Kalpa
the meaning promised in this way
in order to explain in detail
complete with every form of prosperity
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara opens with obeisances to Śrī Gaṇeśa and Śrī Gopāla Kṛṣṇa. In the Third Canto, creation is described through thirty-three chapters: creation arises from the Lord’s glance and the agitation of the guṇas. The first chapter narrates Vidura’s dialogue with Uddhava after he left his relatives. The Bhāgavata was formerly taught by Bhagavān to Brahmā in brief and is now spoken again in Śeṣa’s extensive line. Its transmission is twofold: a concise line through Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Nārada and others, and an extensive line through Śeṣa, Sanatkumāra, Sāṅkhyāyana and others. Through the Nārāyaṇa–Brahmā dialogue it is taught by the four verses beginning ‘I alone existed’; through the Brahmā–Nārada dialogue it is expanded as the ten characteristics; and, to state it in great detail as spoken by Śeṣa, the Third Canto begins. Śrīdhara then outlines its thirty-three chapters and recalls the promise to explain the measure of time and the Pādma Kalpa. Śukadeva therefore introduces the history, complete with all prosperity.

entries.sanskrit: किं चातिश्लाघ्यं त्यागानर्हम् इत्य् आह---यद् वै प्रसिद्धं गृहं वः पाण्डवानां मन्त्र-कृद् दौत्य-कर्ता सन्न् अयं श्री-कृष्णः । बुद्धि-सन्निधानाद् अयम् इति निर्देशः । पौरवेन्द्रो दुर्योधनस् तस्य गृहं हित्वानाहूत एव प्रविवेश । तत्र हेतुः---आत्म-सात्-कृतम् आत्मीयत्वेन गृहीतम् ॥२॥
word_for_word: the maker of counsel, the performer of a diplomatic mission
this Śrī Kṛṣṇa being [such a one]
‘this one’ is the designation because intelligence is present
taken as one’s own, accepted as one’s own
entries.literal_english: Moreover, Śrīdhara explains why a house not fit to be abandoned was nevertheless abandoned. The well-known house of the Pāṇḍavas was the house in which Śrī Kṛṣṇa acted as counsellor and envoy. ‘This one’ is said because He is present with intelligence. Duryodhana, king of the Pauravas, entered that house uninvited after abandoning his own; the reason is that it had been accepted as one’s own.

entries.sanskrit: वरीयसि श्रेष्ठे । अल्पस्यार्थस्योदयो यस्मात् तथाभूतो न भवति । साधु-वादेन सताम् अनुमोदनेनोपबृंहितः संवर्धितः । यद्वा, साधोर् मैत्रेयस्य वादेनोत्तरेण श्लाघित इत्य् अर्थः ॥४॥
word_for_word: because it does not arise from a matter of little importance
strengthened by the approval of good people
यद्वा साधोर् मैत्रेयस्य वादेनोत्तरेण श्लाघित इत्य् अर्थः
or, praised by the answer of the saintly Maitreya
entries.literal_english: “Variyasi” means excellent. The question is not about any small matter; it is strengthened by the approval of virtuous people. Alternatively, it is praised by the response of the saintly Maitreya.

entries.sanskrit: त्यागानर्हस्यापि गृहस्य त्यागे हेतुत्वेन कौरवापराधान् आह---यदेत्य् एकादशभिः । एतेषां च तदा स क्षत्ता अयाद् इत्य् एकादशे क्रिया-सम्बन्धः । यविष्ठस्य कनिष्ठस्य पाण्डोः । विबन्धून् पितृ-हीनान् ॥६॥
word_for_word: as the cause for abandoning even a house unfit to be abandoned
he states the offenses of the Kauravas
eteṣāṃ ca tadā sa kṣattā ayād iti
and the action ‘then Vidura departed’ is connected with these
connected with the verb in the eleventh
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara states the Kauravas’ offenses as the cause for abandoning even a house that ought not to be abandoned. The verses beginning with ‘yad’ are eleven in number, and the verb ‘then Vidura departed’ in the eleventh is connected with them. ‘Yaviṣṭhasya’ means the younger Pāṇḍu, and ‘vibandhūn’ means fatherless, without a protector.

entries.sanskrit: कुरु-देवस्य युधिष्ठिरस्य देव्या द्रौपद्या आत्मनः स्नुषायाः स्वीयैर् अस्रैर् अश्रुभिः स्व-कुच-कुङ्कुमानि रिपु-स्त्रीणां वा तद्-भर्तृ-वधेन हरन्त्याः ॥७॥
word_for_word: of Yudhiṣṭhira, the lord of the Kurus
wiping away the vermilion from her breasts
by the killing of their husbands
entries.literal_english: Draupadī is the queen of Yudhiṣṭhira, the lord of the Kurus. The verse refers to her own tears wiping away the vermilion from her breasts, or to the vermilion of the enemy women being wiped away by the killing of their husbands.

सत्यावलम्बस्य सत्याश्रयस्य वनात् प्रत्यागतस्य समयेन पूर्व-कृतेन दायम् अंशं याचमानस्य यद् यदा नादान् न ददौ । तमो मोहं जुषाणः \[पुत्रं सेवमानः, अविवेकं वा\][^२] ॥८॥

[^२]: "पुत्रम्॥।वा" इति क्वाचित्कः पाठः ।
word_for_word: of one supported by truth, whose refuge is truth
who had returned from the forest
the share previously assigned, at the proper time
when he did not give what was requested
entries.literal_english: The verse concerns one supported by truth who had returned from the forest and, at the proper time, asked for the share previously assigned to him. When it was not given, Dhṛtarāṣṭra embraced darkness and delusion by serving his son, or, according to the alternative reading, by lacking discrimination.

entries.sanskrit: यानि वचनानि पुंसां भीष्मादीनाम् अमृतायनान्य् अमृत-स्रावीणि राजा धृतराष्ट्रो दुर्योधनो वा उरु बहु न मेने । क्षतो नष्टः पुण्य-लेशो यस्य सः । न सुख-कीर्ति-धर्मादि-हेतुः, किन्तु राज्य-प्राप्ति-मात्र-हेतुः पुण्य-लेश एवासीत् । तस्यापि नष्टत्वाद् अनादृतवान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥९॥
word_for_word: he whose remnant of merit was destroyed
not a cause of happiness, fame, dharma and the rest
but merely a cause of obtaining the kingdom
there was only a remnant of merit
he did not respect them; that is the meaning
entries.literal_english: The words of Bhīṣma and the others were nectar-bearing and led toward immortality, yet Dhṛtarāṣṭra or Duryodhana did not esteem them highly. Their remaining merit was destroyed: it was not a cause of happiness, fame or dharma, but only a remnant of merit that could obtain the kingdom. Since even that remnant was destroyed, he disregarded their words.

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं विदुरस्यैव कृतं पराभवं दर्शयति---यदा इत्य्-आदि-षड्भिः । यदा पूर्वजेन धृतराष्ट्रेण मन्त्राय च उपहूतोऽन्तर्-गृहं प्रविष्टो मन्त्रं पृष्टः सन्न्, अथानन्तरं तद् आह । किं मन्त्रिणोऽद्यापि यद् वैदुरिकं विदुर-वाक्यम् इति प्रसिद्धं वदन्ति ॥१०॥
word_for_word: idānīm vidurasya eva kṛtam parābhavam darśayati
now he shows the defeat and humiliation inflicted on Vidura
yad vaidurikam vidura-vākyam iti prasiddham vadanti
call ‘Vaidurīka’, the speech of Vidura; this is well known
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara now displays the humiliation inflicted on Vidura, in the six verses beginning with ‘yadā’. Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura’s elder brother, invited him into the inner house for counsel and asked him for advice. The expression means that even today advisers call Vidura’s speech ‘Vaidurīka’; this is the established usage.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवाह---अजात-शत्रोर् इति त्रिभिः । तव आगोऽपराधं सहमानस्य दायं प्रतियच्छ देहि । यत्रापराधेऽनुजैः सह वर्तमानो वृकोदर-रूपोऽहिः क्रोधेन श्वसन् वर्तते । यद् यस्मात् त्वम् अलम् अत्यर्थं बिभेषि ॥११॥
word_for_word: of you who endure your offense
in the matter of that offense
existing together with the younger brothers
a serpent in the form of Bhīma
yad yasmāt tvam alam atyartham bibheṣi
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the three verses beginning with ‘ajāta-śatroḥ’. The meaning is: return the inheritance to you, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who are enduring the offense. In this offense Bhīma, who is like a serpent and lives with the younger brothers, remains breathing with anger; therefore you are exceedingly afraid.

entries.sanskrit: ननु मम तादृशाः पुत्रा बहवः सन्तीति गर्वं मा कृथा इत्य् आह---पार्थांस् तु मुकुन्द आत्मीयत्वेन गृहीतवान् । स च देवस् तत्रापि भगवान् न तु प्राकृतः । किं च, सह क्षिति-देवैर् विप्रैर् देवैश् चेन्द्रादिभिर् वर्तमानः । यतोऽसौ तत्रैव विप्रा देवाश् चेत्य् अर्थः । स च स्व-पुर्याम् एव सुखम् आस्ते, न त्व् अन्यत्र गतः । किं च, यदु-देवानां देवः पूज्यः । यतोऽसौ तत्रैव सर्वे राजानः । अतः पार्थानां दायं देहीति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: nanu mama tādṛśāḥ putrāḥ bahavaḥ santi
‘Surely I have many sons like that’
but Mukunda has accepted the Pāṇḍavas as His own
saḥ ca devaḥ tatra api bhagavān
and He is divine, there also Bhagavān
kṣiti-devaiḥ vipraiḥ devaiḥ ca indra-ādibhiḥ saha vartamānaḥ
existing together with the earth-gods, brāhmaṇas, and gods beginning with Indra
saḥ ca sva-puryām eva sukham āste
and He remains happily in His own city
the worshipful Lord of the Yadu lords
yataḥ asau tatra eva sarve rājānaḥ
because all the kings are there
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara warns Dhṛtarāṣṭra not to become proud by thinking, ‘I have many sons like that.’ Mukunda has accepted the Pāṇḍavas as His own. He is divine and Bhagavān, not material, and is present with the brāhmaṇas and gods headed by Indra. He remains happily in His own city, worshipped as the Lord of the Yadu lords, where all the kings are present. Therefore, give the Pāṇḍavas their share.

transliteration: nanu mama tādṛśāḥ putrā bahavaḥ santīti garvaṃ mā kṛthā ity āha---pārthāṃs tu mukunda ātmīyatvena gṛhītavān | sa ca devas tatrāpi bhagavān na tu prākṛtaḥ | kiṃ ca, saha kṣiti-devair viprair devaiś cendrādibhir vartamānaḥ | yato’sau tatraiva viprā devāś cety arthaḥ | sa ca sva-puryām eva sukham āste, na tv anyatra gataḥ | kiṃ ca, yadu-devānāṃ devaḥ pūjyaḥ | yato’sau tatraiva sarve rājānaḥ | ataḥ pārthānāṃ dāyaṃ dehīti ||12||

entries.sanskrit:
दुर्योधनस् तन् न मन्यत इति चेद् अत आह---स एष मूर्तो दोष एव गृहान् प्रविष्ट आस्ते । दोषत्वे हेतुः\--पुरुष-द्विट् श्री-कृष्ण-द्वेष्टा । कोऽसौ ? यं त्वम् अपत्य-मत्या पुष्णासि न त्व् अपत्यम् असौ । न पतत्य् अस्माद् इति ह्य् अपत्यं प्राहुः । गता श्रीर् यस्मात् स त्वम् इत्य् आक्रोशति । अत एनम् अशैवम् अमङ्गलम् आशु त्यज । कथं पुत्रस् त्याज्यः ? तत्राह---कुलस्य कौशलाय, त्यजेद् एकं कुलस्यार्थे[^३] \[हितोपदेश १.१४३\] इति हि न्यायः ॥१३॥

[^३]: त्यजेद् एकं कुलस्यार्थे ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।

    ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥
word_for_word: duryodhanas tan na manyata iti cet
if Duryodhana does not accept that
a hater of persons, a hater of Śrī Kṛṣṇa
whom you nourish, thinking him a child
but he is not a child
na patati asmāt iti apatyam prāhuḥ
they call ‘apatya’ one from whom [the father] does not fall
you are one from whom fortune has departed
ataḥ enam aśaivam amaṅgalam āśu tyaja
therefore quickly abandon this inauspicious one
for the welfare of the family
one should abandon one for the sake of the family
one should abandon a family for the sake of a village
grāmam janapadasya arthe ātma-arthe pṛthivīm tyajet
one should abandon a village for a district, and the earth for one’s own sake
entries.literal_english: If [one says], “Duryodhana does not accept that,” then: “This very embodied fault has entered the house and remains.” The reason he is a fault: he hates men—he hates Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Who is this? The one whom you nourish, thinking him a son; he is not an offspring. They call an offspring one from whom [the father] does not fall away. Since your fortune has departed, he reproaches you: “You!” Therefore quickly abandon this unprosperous, inauspicious one. How can a son be abandoned? [The answer:] “For the welfare of the family”—this is indeed the rule: “One should give up one for the sake of the family; for the sake of a village, one should give up a family; for the sake of a district, one should give up a village; for oneself, one should give up the earth.”

entries.sanskrit: इत्य् ऊचिवान् एवं उक्तवान् । असौ क्षत्ता विदुरः सतां स्पृहणीयं शीलं यस्य स कर्ण-दुःशासन-शकुनि-सहितेन दुर्योधनेन असत्-कृतस् तिरस्-कृतः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: whose character is desired by the virtuous
by Duryodhana together with Karṇa, Duḥśāsana and Śakuni
entries.literal_english: Having spoken thus, Vidura—whose character is desired by the virtuous—was disrespected and insulted by Duryodhana together with Karṇa, Duḥśāsana and Śakuni.

entries.sanskrit: तिरस्कारम् आह---क इति । दासी-सुतो ह्य् अत्राह्वानानर्हः । जिह्मश् च कुटिलः । जिह्मताम् अह---यस्य बलिना अन्नेन पुष्टस् तस्मिन्न् एव प्रतीपः प्रतिकूलः परेषां कार्ये वर्तते । अतः पुरान् निर्वास्यताम् । श्वसानः श्वसन् जीव-मात्र-शेष इत्य् अर्थः । पाठान्तरे श्मशान-वद् अमङ्गलः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: a son of a maidservant, unfit to be invited here
he acts in the affairs of others
therefore let him be expelled from the cities
meaning that only a remnant of life remains
according to another reading, inauspicious like a cremation ground
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the insult: Vidura is called ‘ka’, a son of a maidservant and therefore unfit to be invited, and ‘jihma’, crooked. Though nourished by Duryodhana’s powerful food, he acts against that very person in the affairs of others. Therefore he is told to be expelled from the cities. ‘Breathing’ means that only a remnant of life remains; another reading makes him inauspicious like a cremation ground.

transliteration: tiraskāram āha---ka iti | dāsī-suto hy atrāhvānānarhaḥ | jihmaś ca kuṭilaḥ | jihmatām aha---yasya balinā annena puṣṭas tasminn eva pratīpaḥ pratikūlaḥ pareṣāṃ kārye vartate | ataḥ purān nirvāsyatām | śvasānaḥ śvasan jīva-mātra-śeṣa ity arthaḥ | pāṭhāntare śmaśāna-vad amaṅgalaḥ ||15||

entries.sanskrit: अत्युल्बणैः कर्णयोर् बाणवत् प्रविशद्भिः परुष-वाक्यैर् मर्मसु ताडितोऽपि गत-व्यथः । तत्र हेतुः---मायां उरु बहु मानयन्न् "अहो मायाया माहात्म्यम्" इति ताम् एव तत्र हेतुं मन्यमानस् तन्-निःसारणात् पूर्वं स्वयम् एव अयान् निर्जगाम । किं कृत्वा ? "एते नूनं मरिष्यन्ति, किं धनुषा ?" इति तस्य द्वारि धनुर् निधाय । यद् वा, "भीमादिभिः सङ्गत्यास्माभिर् योत्स्यतीति मा शङ्कीः" इति धनुर्-निधानम् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: although struck in the vital places
considering that alone the cause there
he himself went out and departed
placing his bow at his door
he will fight us after joining Bhīma and the others
entries.literal_english: Though Vidura was struck in his vital places by extremely harsh words entering his ears like arrows, he was free from pain. Śrīdhara gives the reason: he greatly honoured Māyā, thinking, ‘Ah, such is the power of Māyā,’ and regarded that Māyā as the cause of what was happening. Before the wicked men could expel him, he departed of his own accord. He placed his bow at the door, thinking, ‘These men will surely die—what use is a bow?’ Alternatively, he placed it there to say, ‘Do not suspect that I will join Bhīma and the others and fight you.’

transliteration: atyulbaṇaiḥ karṇayor bāṇavat praviśadbhiḥ paruṣa-vākyair marmasu tāḍito’pi gata-vyathaḥ | tatra hetuḥ---māyāṃ uru bahu mānayann "aho māyāyā māhātmyam" iti tām eva tatra hetuṃ manyamānas tan-niḥsāraṇāt pūrvaṃ svayam eva ayān nirjagāma | kiṃ kṛtvā ? "ete nūnaṃ mariṣyanti, kiṃ dhanuṣā ?" iti tasya dvāri dhanur nidhāya | yad vā, "bhīmādibhiḥ saṅgatyāsmābhir yotsyatīti mā śaṅkīḥ" iti dhanur-nidhānam ||16|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : "svayam" ity atra "smayan"[^5] iti citsukhaḥ ||16|| [^5]: smayad iti pāṭhāntaraḥ| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : sa ittham atyulbaṇa-karṇa-bāṇaiḥ atyulbaṇaiḥ paruṣa-vākyair karṇayor bāṇair iva praviśya marma-sthāneṣu tāḍitaḥ | tatrāpi bhrātuḥ puraḥ, "are kim evaṃ brūṣe ?" ity apy anuktavataḥ | kiṃ ca, tāḍito’pi gata-vyathaḥ | "dhanyo’si are duryodhana, dhanyo’si tvayā mama sarvā api vyathā nirvāpitā yad ito niḥsāryamāṇasya dūre kvacana tīrthādiṣu nirviṇṇatayā sthāsyatas tvaj-janake mamatāṃ tyaktavato mama kā vyathā ?" iti manasy anulapyeti bhāvaḥ | ayāt nirjagāma svayam iti duṣṭair niḥsāraṇāt svayam eva niḥsaraṇaṃ bhadram iti bhāvaḥ | dhanur-dvāri nidhāya iti "samprati sarvaṃ sva-gṛhādikam api tyaktavato vivikte kvacid upaviśya kṛṣṇaṃ bhajiṣyato mama kim anena duścihnena dhanuṣā ?" iti bhāvaḥ | yad vā, "bhīmādibhiḥ saṅgatyāsmābhiḥ saha yotsyata iti pāpo’yaṃ mā śaṅketa" iti dhanur-nidhānam | māyāṃ uru mānayānaḥ mānayann iti māyayaivāndhīkṛtaḥ puraḥ santam api kṛṣṇaṃ na paśyati| yad vā, aho māyā-māhātmyaṃ bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇasya yad evaṃ prakāreṇa māṃ sva-bhaktam ito niṣkāśya bhīmādibhir niḥsaṃśayam ete ghātayiṣyanta iti ||16|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: ततो निर्गतस्य तीर्थाटन-प्रकारम् आह---स इत्य् अष्टभिः । स गजाह्वयान् निर्गतः संस् तीर्थं पादौ यस्य तस्य हरेः पदानि क्षेत्राणि पुण्य-चिकीर्षयाऽन्वाक्रमत् प्रत्यपद्यत। कौरवाणां पुण्येन लब्ध इति तेषां भाग्यम् एव तेन रूपेण गतम् इति सूचितम् । उर्व्यां सहस्र-मूर्तिर् ब्रह्म-रुद्राद्य्-अनेक-मूर्तिः संस् तीर्थ-पाद्यानि यान्य् अधिष्ठाय स्थितः तानि तानि जगामेत्य् अर्थः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: then, of the one who had departed
he explains the manner of pilgrimage
of Hari, whose feet are the sacred places
the sacred fields are the steps/feet
with the desire to gain merit
obtained through the merit of the Kauravas
teṣāṃ bhāgyam eva tena rūpeṇa gatam
their fortune itself went in that form
having a thousand forms upon the earth
being of many forms beginning with Brahmā and Rudra
whatever places are the feet of the sacred ford
he went to each of them
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara now explains the manner of pilgrimage of the one who had departed. In the eight verses beginning with ‘saḥ’, Vidura leaves Hastināpura and approaches the sacred fields that are Hari’s feet, desiring to gain merit. It is implied that the fortune obtained by the Kauravas through their merit itself travelled in this form. Hari, who has a thousand forms on earth and many forms beginning with Brahmā and Rudra, is present in those sacred places; Vidura went to each of them.

transliteration: tato nirgatasya tīrthāṭana-prakāram āha---sa ity aṣṭabhiḥ | sa gajāhvayān nirgataḥ saṃs tīrthaṃ pādau yasya tasya hareḥ padāni kṣetrāṇi puṇya-cikīrṣayā’nvākramat pratyapadyata| kauravāṇāṃ puṇyena labdha iti teṣāṃ bhāgyam eva tena rūpeṇa gatam iti sūcitam | urvyāṃ sahasra-mūrtir brahma-rudrādy-aneka-mūrtiḥ saṃs tīrtha-pādyāni yāny adhiṣṭhāya sthitaḥ tāni tāni jagāmety arthaḥ ||17|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : anvākramat anukrameṇa prāpa | puṇya-cikīrṣayā tad-duḥsaṅga-prāyaścittecchayā | ataḥ sa-doṣaṃ-manyaḥ sahasā śrī-kṛṣṇam api draṣṭuṃ na jagāmeti bhāvaḥ ||17|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : kuros tad-vaṃśyānāṃ ca puṇyena labdha iti teṣāṃ bhāgyam eva tena rūpeṇa gatam iti sūcitam | tīrthaṃ pādau yasya tasya harer iti tac-caraṇa-buddhyaiva tādṛśānāṃ tīrtha-didṛkṣeti sūcitam | padāni kṣetrāṇi sahasra-mūrtir matsya-kūrmādy-aneka-mūrtiḥ san yāni yāny adhiṣṭhāya sthitaḥ ||17|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: पुण्यानि यान्य् उपवनादीनि तेषु कुञ्जं लतादि-गूढ-स्थानम् । अपङ्कानि तोयानि येषां तेषु सरित्-सरःसु च तीर्थेष्व् आयतनेषु क्षेत्रेषु च । कीदृशेषु ? अनन्तस्य लिङ्गैर् मूर्तिभिः सम्यग् अलङ्कृतेषु । अनन्य एकाकी ॥१८॥
word_for_word: the meritorious gardens and such places
a hidden place of creepers and the like
in sacred places, shrines and holy fields
with the forms that are marks of Ananta
entries.literal_english: The meritorious places were gardens and the like, including groves and hidden places covered by creepers. They were rivers and lakes whose waters were without mud, and sacred places, shrines and holy fields properly adorned with the forms that manifest Ananta. Vidura was alone and solitary.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: puṇyāni yāny upavanādīni teṣu kuñjaṃ latādi-gūḍha-sthānam | apaṅkāni toyāni yeṣāṃ teṣu sarit-saraḥsu ca tīrtheṣv āyataneṣu kṣetreṣu ca | kīdṛśeṣu ? anantasya liṅgair mūrtibhiḥ samyag alaṅkṛteṣu | ananya ekākī ||18|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : pureṣu prasiddheṣu na vidyate paṅkaṃ pāpaṃ yebhyas teṣu pāpa-hantṛṣu toyeṣu ananyaḥ sarvatra śrī-kṛṣṇaika-dṛṣṭiḥ ||18|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : ananya ekākī ||18|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: किं च, गां पर्यटन् व्रतानि चेरे आचरत् । मेध्या पवित्रा विविक्तासङ्कीर्णा वृत्तिर् जीविका यस्य । सदाप्लुतः प्रति-तीर्थं स्नातः । अधः शयनं यस्य । अवधूतोऽसंस्कृत-देहः, अवधूत-वेषो वल्कलादि-धारी । अत एव स्वैर् अलक्षितः ॥१९॥
word_for_word: having bathed at each sacred place
with the dress of an ascetic
entries.literal_english: Moreover, wandering over the earth, Vidura observed vows. His livelihood was pure, secluded and uncrowded; he bathed continually, bathing at every sacred place. He slept on the ground. His body was unadorned, his ascetic dress consisted of bark and the like, and for that very reason he moved freely without being noticed.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: kiṃ ca, gāṃ paryaṭan vratāni cere ācarat | medhyā pavitrā viviktāsaṅkīrṇā vṛttir jīvikā yasya | sadāplutaḥ prati-tīrthaṃ snātaḥ | adhaḥ śayanaṃ yasya | avadhūto’saṃskṛta-dehaḥ, avadhūta-veṣo valkalādi-dhārī | ata eva svair alakṣitaḥ ||19|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : viviktatvaṃ paravṛttibhir amiśratvam ||19|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : gāṃ pṛthivīṃ medhyā pavitrā viviktā vṛttāntareṇāmiśritā vṛtti-jīvikā yasya saḥ | sadāplutaḥ prati-tīrthaṃ snāta itisnānena pāvitryaṃ lakṣyate | snānānantaraṃ kadācid aspṛśya-sparśe punar api snātīti sadā bhagavan-mantrādi-smaraṇārthaṃ pavitra eva tiṣṭhatīty arthaḥ | avadhūto’saṃskṛta-dehaḥ, avadhūta-veṣo valkalādi-dhārī, ata eva svair alakṣitaḥ ||19|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: एकस्यैव चक्रं सैन्यं यस्याम् । एकम् एव राज-चिह्नं श्वेतातपत्रं यस्यां ताम् । अजितेन श्री-कृष्णेन सहायेन ॥२०॥
word_for_word: with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Ajita, as companion
entries.literal_english: The land he traversed had only one wheel as its army and only one royal insignia, the white umbrella. His companion was Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Unconquered.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: ekasyaiva cakraṃ sainyaṃ yasyām | ekam eva rāja-cihnaṃ śvetātapatraṃ yasyāṃ tām | ajitena śrī-kṛṣṇena sahāyena ||20|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : bhāratam eva varṣam iti tan-madhya-varti kumārikā-khaṇḍam eva jñeyaṃ viṣṇu-purāṇānusāreṇānyatrāgamyatvāt ||20|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : ekasyaiva cakraṃ sainyaṃ yasyām | ekam eva rāja-cihnaṃ śvetātapatraṃ yasyāṃ tām | ajitena śrī-kṛṣṇena sahāyena hetunā pārtho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ||20|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: तत्र प्रभासे परस्पर-स्पर्धया निमित्त-भूतया सुहृदां कौरवाणां विनष्टिं विनाशम् अशृणोत् । परस्पर-नाशे दृष्टान्तः---वेणुजं वह्निं संश्रयते यद् वनं, तद् यथा दग्धं भवति, तथा । प्रत्यगुद्गमाभिमुखम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: with mutual rivalry as the cause
the destruction of the Kauravas, his friends
the forest that contains fire born from bamboo
facing the return toward its origin
entries.literal_english: At Prabhāsa, Vidura heard of the destruction of his Kaurava friends, caused by mutual rivalry. For mutual destruction there is an example: a forest that contains fire born from bamboo is burned by that fire; so it was with them. The final expression indicates a turning back toward one’s source.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: tatra prabhāse paraspara-spardhayā nimitta-bhūtayā suhṛdāṃ kauravāṇāṃ vinaṣṭiṃ vināśam aśṛṇot | paraspara-nāśe dṛṣṭāntaḥ---veṇujaṃ vahniṃ saṃśrayate yad vanaṃ, tad yathā dagdhaṃ bhavati, tathā | pratyagudgamābhimukham ||21|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : suhṛd-vinaṣṭim iti | yādavānāṃ vinaṣṭim ity eva jñeyam | nātivilambād evoddhavena milanāt ||21|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : tatra prabhāse suhṛdāṃ kauravāṇāṃ vinaṣṭiṃ vināśam, duryodhanādiṣu sauhārdābhāvād anativilambe evoddhava-milanāc ca suhṛdāṃ yādavānām iti kecid vyācakṣate | vanaṃ yathā dagdhaṃ bhavatīty anvayaḥ | pratyak pratīcīṃ paścima-vāhinīm ity arthaḥ ||21|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: त्रितादीनाम् एकादश-तीर्थानि तत्-तन्-नाम्ना प्रसिद्धान्य् आसेवितवान् ॥२२॥
entries.source_note: Pinned source heading jointly attributes this passage to Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī; exact shared commentary preserved.
transliteration: tritādīnām ekādaśa-tīrthāni tat-tan-nāmnā prasiddhāny āsevitavān ||22||
entries.literal_english: He visited the eleven sacred places of Trita and the others, each renowned by its own name.

entries.sanskrit: द्विज-देवैर् ऋषिभिर् देवैश् च कृतानि । अङ्गम् अङ्गं प्रति वर्तन्ते इति प्रत्यङ्गान्य् आयुधानि तेषु मुख्यं चक्रं तेनाङ्कितानि मूर्धन्य-हेम-कुम्भेषु चिह्नितानि मन्दिराणि, येषु तानि नाना-विधानि विष्णोर् आयतनानि क्षेत्राणि तीर्थानि चासिषेवे । येषां चक्राङ्कित-मन्दिर-वतां दर्शनाच् छ्री-कृष्ण-स्मरणं भवति ॥२३॥
word_for_word: aṅgam aṅgam prati vartante iti pratyaṅgāni āyudhāni
weapons present in each limb are called ‘pratyaṅga’
among them the principal weapon is the discus
temples marked with it on their crowning golden vessels
from seeing temples marked with the discus
entries.literal_english: He visited the various abodes of Viṣṇu—holy fields and sacred places—made by brāhmaṇas and gods. The weapons present in each limb are called ‘pratyaṅga’; among them the principal is the discus, and temples were marked with it on their crowning golden vessels. Seeing such temples marked with the discus produces remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source block restored and glossed.
transliteration: dvija-devair ṛṣibhir devaiś ca kṛtāni | aṅgam aṅgaṃ prati vartante iti pratyaṅgāny āyudhāni teṣu mukhyaṃ cakraṃ tenāṅkitāni mūrdhanya-hema-kumbheṣu cihnitāni mandirāṇi, yeṣu tāni nānā-vidhāni viṣṇor āyatanāni kṣetrāṇi tīrthāni cāsiṣeve | yeṣāṃ cakrāṅkita-mandira-vatāṃ darśanāc chrī-kṛṣṇa-smaraṇaṃ bhavati ||23||

entries.sanskrit: अतिव्रज्य अतिक्रम्य । यावद् उद्धवः प्राप्तः, तावत् स्वयम् अपि यमुनां उपेत्य ॥२४॥
word_for_word: meanwhile he himself also approached the Yamunā
entries.literal_english: ‘Ativrajya’ means ‘having crossed beyond’ or ‘having passed over’. Until Vidura reached Uddhava, he himself also approached the Yamunā.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact source block restored and glossed.
transliteration: ativrajya atikramya | yāvad uddhavaḥ prāptaḥ, tāvat svayam api yamunāṃ upetya ||24||

entries.sanskrit: स विदुरः । प्राक्-तनयं पूर्व-शिष्यं नीति-शास्त्रे । पाठान्तरे प्राप्तो नयो नीति-शास्त्रं येन तम् । प्रतीतं प्रख्यातम् । स्वानां ज्ञातीनां भद्रम् अपृच्छत् । प्रश्ने हेतुः---भगवतः प्रजानां पोष्याणाम् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: a former student in the science of policy
through whom the science of policy [was known]
he asked about the welfare of his relatives
of the Lord’s people who were to be protected
entries.literal_english: This was Vidura. He asked after the welfare of his own relatives. Uddhava is understood as his former student in political science—or, according to another reading, as one who had attained the science of policy through him and was renowned. The reason for Vidura’s question was that these were the Lord’s people, those who were to be protected and nourished.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: sa viduraḥ | prāk-tanayaṃ pūrva-śiṣyaṃ nīti-śāstre | pāṭhāntare prāpto nayo nīti-śāstraṃ yena tam | pratītaṃ prakhyātam | svānāṃ jñātīnāṃ bhadram apṛcchat | praśne hetuḥ---bhagavataḥ prajānāṃ poṣyāṇām ||25|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : suhṛd-vinaṣṭeḥ śrutatve’pi svānāṃ bhadram apṛcchad iti | śokāveśa-svabhāvo’yam | sveṣāṃ paramātmīyānām ||25|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : prāk-tanayaṃ pūrva-śiṣyaṃ nīti-śāstre | prāpta-nayam iti vā pāṭhaḥ | pratītaṃ khyātam, tatra vidura-kartṛkāliṅgane’pi uddhavasya namaskārābhāvaḥ prema-mūrcchayaiva jñeyaḥ ||25|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: प्रथमं तावद् राम-कृष्णयोः कुशलं पृच्छति । कच्चिद् इति प्रश्ने । स्व-नाभौ भवः स्व-नाभ्यः पाद्मो ब्रह्मा, तस्य अनुवृत्त्या प्रार्थनयेह अवतीर्णौ कुशलम् आसाते वर्तते। कृत-क्षणौ दत्तावसरौ सर्वेषां कृतोत्सवाव् इति वा । तयोर् नित्य-कुशलत्वेऽप्य् उक्त-विशेषण-विशिष्टौ शूरसेनस्य गृहे कच्चिद् आसाते ? इति प्रश्नः ॥२६॥
word_for_word: he asks the welfare of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa
the lotus-born Brahmā from His own navel
having descended here at his request
having granted an opportunity to all
or, having made festivals for all
entries.literal_english: First Vidura asks about the welfare of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa. The question uses ‘kaccit’. They are said to have descended here at the request of lotus-born Brahmā, who arose from the Lord’s own navel. ‘Kṛta-kṣaṇau’ may mean that they give everyone an opportunity, or that they make festivals for everyone. Although they are eternally well, Vidura asks whether, possessing these stated qualities, they dwell in the house of Śūrasena.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: prathamaṃ tāvad rāma-kṛṣṇayoḥ kuśalaṃ pṛcchati | kaccid iti praśne | sva-nābhau bhavaḥ sva-nābhyaḥ pādmo brahmā, tasya anuvṛttyā prārthanayeha avatīrṇau kuśalam āsāte vartate| kṛta-kṣaṇau dattāvasarau sarveṣāṃ kṛtotsavāv iti vā | tayor nitya-kuśalatve’py ukta-viśeṣaṇa-viśiṣṭau śūrasenasya gṛhe kaccid āsāte ? iti praśnaḥ ||26|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : sva-nābhyeti | svīyasya garbhoda-śāyino nābhau bhavaḥ sva-nābhyaḥ nija-śāsanārhaṇam itivat vyakhyātam | kuśalaṃ lokānāṃ maṅgalaṃ yasmāt tad yathā syāt ||26|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : bhagavat-prakaṭa-sthityaiva tat-prajānāṃ bhadram iti bhagavat-sukha-sthitiṃ pṛcchati---kaccid iti | praśne sva-nābhau bhavaḥ svanābhyaḥ pādmo brahmā kṛta-kṣaṇau kṛtotsavau, tayor nitya-kuśalinor api kuśala-praśnaḥ premṇaiva jñeyaḥ ||26|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: यदूनां कुशलं पृच्छति नवभिः । भामः पूज्यः । शौरिर् वसुदेवः । यद् वा, भामो भगिनी-भर्ता । कुन्ती वसुदेवस्य भगिनी । अतो देवकी पाण्डोर् भगिनीति लोक-व्यवहारः। वरान् अर्थान् । वदान्योऽत्युदारः । वराणां तत्-पतीनां तर्पणेन सन्तर्पणेन सह ॥२७॥
word_for_word: he asks the welfare of the Yadus in nine verses
or Bhāma is the husband of a sister
the common usage is that Devakī is Pāṇḍu’s sister
by satisfying the lords of the desired things
entries.literal_english: In the next nine verses Vidura asks about the welfare of the Yadus. Śauri is Vasudeva; Bhāma may mean the worshipful one or the husband of a sister. Kuntī was Vasudeva’s sister, and ordinary usage therefore calls Devakī Pāṇḍu’s sister. The desired objects are called ‘varān arthān’; the person is generous and very liberal, together with satisfaction of the lords of those desired things.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: yadūnāṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchati navabhiḥ | bhāmaḥ pūjyaḥ | śaurir vasudevaḥ | yad vā, bhāmo bhaginī-bhartā | kuntī vasudevasya bhaginī | ato devakī pāṇḍor bhaginīti loka-vyavahāraḥ| varān arthān | vadānyo’tyudāraḥ | varāṇāṃ tat-patīnāṃ tarpaṇena santarpaṇena saha ||27|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : bhāmo bhaginī-bhartā, pauravī rohiṇyoḥ patitvāt | svasṝṇām iti kuntī-sneha-tātparyād uktam ||27|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : bhāmo bhaginī-bhartā | vasudeva-bhāryāyāḥ pauravyā vidurādīnāṃ bhaginītvāt śaurir vasudevaḥ | svasṝṇām iti kuntyāḥ snehātiśayo dhvanyate | anyāsu svasṛṣu tathābhāvādṛṣṭeḥ | varān abhīpsitān arthān varāṇāṃ tat-patīnāṃ tarpaṇena santoṣaṇena saha ||27|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: वरूथाधिपतिः सेनानीः । आदि-सर्गे पूर्व-जन्मनि स्मरं कामं सन्तम् अभिलेभे पुत्रं लब्धवती ॥२८॥
word_for_word: in the first creation, the former birth
Kāma, who was present as Smara
she became one who had obtained
entries.literal_english: The commander of the army is meant. In the first creation, that is, in a former birth, she obtained as a son Smara, Kāma, who was present there.

entries.sanskrit: सात्वतादीनाम् अधिप उग्रसेनः । शतपत्र-नेत्रः श्री-कृष्णः । नृपासनाशां राज्याभिलाषं परिहृत्य प्राण-भयेन दूरात् स्थितम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥
word_for_word: Ugrasena, lord of the Sātvatas and others
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose eyes are like lotus petals
the desire for the royal seat
having abandoned the desire for kingship
entries.literal_english: Ugrasena is the lord of the Sātvatas and others. Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the one with lotus-petal eyes. The expression means that he stood far away, having abandoned the desire for the royal throne because of fear for his life.

entries.sanskrit: हे साउम्य । हरेः सुतस् तेन सदृक्षः सदृशः साधु सुखम् आस्ते । गुहं स्वामि-कार्तिकेयम् । अग्रे पूर्व-जन्मनि यो भवान्या गर्भे धृतस् तम् ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: ‘O gentle one’: the son of Hari is similar to Him and fares well. Guha means Lord Kārttikeya, who in a former birth was carried in Bhavānī’s womb.

entries.sanskrit: युयुधानः सात्यकिः । क्षेमं कुशलम् आस्ते । फाल्गुनाद् अर्जुनाल् लब्धं धनुषो रहस्यं येन । तदीयाम् अधोक्षज-सम्बन्धिनीम् ॥३१॥
word_for_word: the secret of the bow, by which
that which belongs to him, related to Adhokṣaja
entries.literal_english: Yuyudhāna is Sātyaki, and he fares well. He obtained from Arjuna, Phālguna, the secret of the bow. The final phrase refers to what belongs to him and is connected with Adhokṣaja.

entries.sanskrit: श्वफल्क-पुत्रोऽक्रूरः । बुधो विद्वान् । अतो भगवन्तं प्रपन्नोऽनुसृतः । अत एव अनमीवो निष्पापः, भक्तौ लिङ्गम् । योऽचेष्टत व्यलुठत् । प्रेम्णा विभिन्नं विदीर्णं धैर्यं यस्य सः । स्वस्ति क्षेमम् आस्ते ॥३२॥
word_for_word: therefore surrendered to Bhagavān and followed Him
premṇā vibhinnam vidīrṇam dhairyam yasya saḥ
whose composure was broken and torn apart by love
entries.literal_english: Akrūra is the son of Śvaphalka. He is learned; therefore he surrendered to Bhagavān and followed Him. Being free from affliction and sin is a sign of devotion. He moved and rolled about, his composure broken by love. He is well and secure.

entries.sanskrit: देवक-नामा यो भोजस् तस्य पुत्र्या देवक्याः । विष्णुः प्रजा पुत्रो यस्यास् तस्याः देव-मातुर् अदितेर् इव । कच्चिच् छिवम् । यज्ञ-वितान-रूपम् अर्थं त्रयी यथा प्रकाशकतया बिभर्ति तथा दधार ॥३३॥
word_for_word: of her, like Aditi, the mother of the gods
the meaning in the form of the sacrificial arrangement
as the three Vedas bear it by making it manifest
she bore Him in that way
entries.literal_english: Devakī is the daughter of the Bhoja named Devaka. Viṣṇu is her son, just as He is the son of Aditi, the mother of the gods. Vidura asks whether she is well. She bore Him as the three Vedas bear the meaning of the sacrificial arrangement by making it manifest.

entries.sanskrit:
सात्वतानां उपासकानां कामान् दोग्धि पूरयतीति काम-दुघः । भगवत्त्वे हेतुः---यं शब्दस्य शास्त्रस्य योनिं कारणम् आमनन्ति वेदाः । कुतः ? मनो-मयं मनसः प्रवर्तकम् । तत् कुतः ? सत्त्वस्यान्तः-करणस्य चतुर्-विधस्य तुरीयं तत्त्वं चतुर्थम् अधिदैवम् । चित्ताहङ्कार-बुद्धि-मनसाम् अन्तः-करण-भेदानां क्रमेण वासुदेव-सङ्कर्षण-प्रद्युम्नानिरुद्धा ह्य् अधिष्ठातारः । मनसश् च शब्द-योनित्वं प्रसिद्धम्---मनः पूर्व-रूपम् । वाग् उत्तर-रूपम् इति । तथा अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा मनो-मयःइति प्रस्तुत्य तस्य यजुर् एव शिरः । ऋग् दक्षिणः पक्षः । सामोत्तरः पक्षः\[तै।उ। २.१\] इत्य्-आदि-श्रुतेः । तथा च शिक्षायां---

> आत्मा बुद्ध्या समेत्यार्थान् मनो युङ्क्तेवि वक्षया । >
> मनः कायाग्निम् आहन्ति स प्रेरयति मारुतम् । >
> मारुतस् तूरसि चरन् मन्द्रं जनयति स्वरम् ॥ इत्य्-आदि ॥३४॥
word_for_word: sātvatānām upāsakānām kāmān dogdhi pūrayati iti kāma-dughaḥ
the fulfiller who yields and completes the desires of the worshipping Sātvatas
yam śabdasya śāstrasya yonim kāraṇam āmananti vedāḥ
whom the Vedas declare to be the source and cause of word and scripture
consisting of mind, the impeller of mind
sattvasya antaḥ-karaṇasya catur-vidhasya turīyam tattvam caturtham adhidaivam
the fourth principle and presiding deity of the fourfold inner organ of sattva
of the divisions of the inner organ—mind-stuff, ego, intellect and mind
Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha are the presiding deities
the mind’s being the source of speech is well known
mind is the prior form, speech the later form
the inner self is another, consisting of mind
yajuḥ eva śiraḥ ṛk dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ sāma uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ
the Yajur is its head, Ṛg its right wing, and Sāma its left wing
ātmā buddhyā sametya arthān manaḥ yuṅkte
the self, joining with the intellect, connects the mind to objects
manaḥ kāya-agnim āhanti saḥ prerayati mārutam
the mind strikes the bodily fire, and it impels the breath
mārutaḥ ūrasi caran mandram janayati svaram
the breath moving in the chest produces a deep sound
entries.literal_english: The phrase ‘source of all desires’ means one who yields and fulfils the desires of the Sātvata worshippers. Śrīdhara explains Bhagavān’s status: the Vedas declare Him the source and cause of speech and scripture, the impeller of mind. He is the fourth principle and presiding deity of the fourfold inner organ—mind-stuff, ego, intellect and mind—whose presiding deities are Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. The mind is well known as the source of speech: mind is the prior form and speech the later. The cited Upaniṣadic teaching assigns the Yajur to the head, Ṛg to the right wing and Sāma to the left. The cited phonetic teaching describes the self joining with intellect, the mind striking the bodily fire, the breath being impelled, and that breath producing a deep sound in the chest.

entries.sanskrit: अपि स्वित् किं स्वित् । अन्ये च स्वस्ति चरन्ति । निजस्य देहादि-व्यतिरिक्तस्यात्मनो दैवं श्री-कृष्णम् अनन्य-वृत्त्यैकान्त-भक्ति-भवेन ये सम्यग् अनुव्रताः अनुसृताः । हृदीकश् च सत्यभामाया आत्मजश् च चारुदेष्णश् च गदश् चादिर् येषां तेऽपि ॥३५॥
word_for_word: of the self distinct from one’s body and the rest
entries.literal_english: Vidura asks whether the others also fare well—those who properly follow Śrī Kṛṣṇa as the deity of the self, distinct from the body and the rest, through exclusive single-minded devotion. Hṛdīka, the son of Satyabhāmā, Cārudeṣṇa, Gada and others are included.

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं कुरून् पृच्छति षड्भिः । अपि किम् । स्व-दोर्भ्यां स्व-बाहुवद् वर्तमानाभ्यां विजयाच्युताभ्याम् अर्जुन-कृष्णाभ्यां धर्म-मार्गेण धर्मो युधिष्ठिरः सेतुं धर्म-मर्यादां परिपाति । यस्य सभायां विजयानुवृत्त्या जय-परम्परया, अर्जुनस्य सेवयेति वा । एवं-भूतं यस्यैश्वर्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३६॥
word_for_word: now he asks about the Kurus in six verses
with his own two arms, functioning like his own arms
with Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa, Vijaya and Acyuta
protects the bridge and boundary of dharma
through Arjuna’s attendance, through a succession of victories
whose majesty is of this kind
entries.literal_english: Vidura now asks about the Kurus in six verses. Yudhiṣṭhira, who is Dharma, protects the bridge and boundary of dharma by the path of righteousness, with Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa—Vijaya and Acyuta—functioning as his own two arms. The expression may refer to his assembly’s succession of victories through Arjuna’s presence, or to Arjuna’s service; such is his majesty.

entries.sanskrit: कृताघेषु कृतापराधेषु कुरुषु स्व-कर्तृकम् अघं दीर्घतमं बहु-कालानुचिन्तितम् अहिवद् अत्यमर्षी भीमः किं व्यमुञ्चन् नो वा ? गदाया विचित्रं विविधं मार्गं चरतः ॥३७॥
word_for_word: toward the Kurus who committed offenses
very long, contemplated for a long time
Bhīma, extremely intolerant like a serpent
has he released it or not?
moving through the various, remarkable paths of the mace
entries.literal_english: The Kurus had committed offenses; their own sin had been contemplated for a long time. Did Bhīma, extremely intolerant like a serpent, release [his anger] or not, while moving through the varied and remarkable courses of mace-fighting?

entries.sanskrit: रथ-यूथपानां मध्ये यशो-धाः कीर्ति-धारी । यद् वा, स्वीयानां तेषां कीर्ति-प्रदः उपरता अरयो यस्मात् । यस्य शर-कूटेन बाण-समूहेन गूढ आच्छन्नः ॥३८॥
word_for_word: among the leaders of chariot divisions
or the giver of fame to his own people
entries.literal_english: He is the bearer of fame among the leaders of chariot divisions; or he is the giver of fame to his own people because their enemies had ceased. He was hidden and covered by the mass of his arrows.

entries.sanskrit: उत स्वित् किं स्वित् । यमौ नकुल-सहदेवौ । रेमाते क्रीडाते इत्य् अर्थः । माद्र्याः सुताव् अपि पृथायास् तनयौ पृथायाः पुत्रैर् वृतौ सुपर्णाव् इव रेमाते । किं कृत्वा ? परात् दुर्योधनात् स्व-रिक्थं स्वीयं राज्यं उद्दाय आच्छिद्य । वज्रि-वक्त्राद् इन्द्रस्य मुखात् स्व-रिक्थम् अमृतं गरुड इवेति । यद् वा, सुपर्णाव् इव इति । यदि द्वौ गरुडाव् अमृतम् आनयेतां तर्हि तद्वत् । अक्षिणीव इति मणीवादि-गणत्वात् सन्धिः ॥३९॥
word_for_word: the two sons of Mādrī also
surrounded by the sons of Pṛthā
having taken and seized their own inheritance
from the mouth of Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt
their inheritance like nectar, as Garuḍa [took nectar]
if two Garuḍas were to bring nectar
the sandhi is due to its being in the class of ‘maṇi’ and similar words
entries.literal_english: Or perhaps Vidura asks whether the twins Nakula and Sahadeva are playing. The two sons of Mādrī, surrounded by Pṛthā’s sons, play like two great birds. They did so after taking their own inheritance from the enemy Duryodhana. Śrīdhara compares this to Garuḍa taking nectar from Indra, or to two Garuḍas bringing nectar. The final grammatical note explains the sandhi in the expression ‘like two eyes’ by its belonging to the class of words such as maṇi.

entries.sanskrit: पृथायाः किं नु कुशलं पृच्छेयम्, यतस् तस्याः पाण्डुना विना प्राण-धारणम् एवाश्चर्यम् इत्य् आह---अहो इति । ध्रियते जीवति । न चात्याश्चर्यम् । यतोऽर्भकार्थे ध्रियते न भोगार्थम् । तथापि त्वाश्चर्यम् एवेत्य् आह---तेन तथा-भूतेन विना । तद् एवाह---यस् त्व् इति । धनुर् एव द्वितीयं सहायो यस्य ॥४०॥
word_for_word: what welfare of Pṛthā should I ask?
the maintenance of life itself is astonishing
and it is not exceedingly astonishing
she is sustained for the sake of the children
not for the sake of enjoyment
without that person who was such
whose second companion was only the bow
entries.literal_english: What welfare of Pṛthā should I ask about? Her maintaining life without Pāṇḍu is itself astonishing. Yet it is not completely astonishing, because she lives for the sake of the children, not for enjoyment. Nevertheless it is astonishing that she lives without such a husband, whose second companion was the bow.

entries.sanskrit: पृथा अर्भकार्थे जीवतीति युक्तम् एवेत्य् आह---हे सौम्य, तं धृतराष्ट्रं जिवन् तम् अनुशोचामि । तत् किं ? अधः-पतन्तम् । तत्र हेतुः, परेताय मृताय भ्रात्रे पाण्डवे तत्-पुत्र-द्रोहेण यो विदुद्रुहे द्रोहं कृतवान् । किं च, जीवतोऽपि भ्रातुर् ममापकृतवान् इत्य् आह---येन सुहृद् भ्राताहं स्व-पुर्याः सकाशान् निर्यापितो विवासितः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: Pṛthā lives for the sake of the children
I lament that Dhṛtarāṣṭra is living
for his brother Pāṇḍu, who had died
even though his brother was alive
by whom I, a friendly brother
was driven away and exiled from my own city
entries.literal_english: It is fitting that Pṛthā lives for the sake of the children. But, O gentle one, I lament Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who is still living and falling downward. He betrayed his dead brother Pāṇḍu through hostility toward Pāṇḍu’s sons; moreover, he harmed me although I was his living brother and friend, driving me from my own city into exile.

transliteration: pṛthā arbhakārthe jīvatīti yuktam evety āha---he saumya, taṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ jivan tam anuśocāmi | tat kiṃ ? adhaḥ-patantam | tatra hetuḥ, paretāya mṛtāya bhrātre pāṇḍave tat-putra-droheṇa yo vidudruhe drohaṃ kṛtavān | kiṃ ca, jīvato’pi bhrātur mamāpakṛtavān ity āha---yena suhṛd bhrātāhaṃ sva-puryāḥ sakāśān niryāpito vivāsitaḥ ||41|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : tad evam ajīvantaṃ pāṇḍuṃ na śocāmi sad-gaty-arhatvāt, dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ tu jīvantam api tad-vaiparītyāc chocāmy evety āha---somyeti ||41|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : dhṛtarāṣṭrasyāndhasya tu kuśalaṃ naiva pṛcchāmi, kintu tam adhaḥ-patantam anuśoce---he saumya uddhava ! yaḥ paretāya mṛtāyāpi bhrātre tat-putra-droheṇa vidudruhe drohaṃ kṛtavān mahyam aparasmai bhrātre jīvate’pi vidudruhe ity āha---niryāpita iti suhṛt tasya hita-kāry api ||41|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: अहो स्वलु विस्मयो जानतोऽपि तस्यैवं दुश्चेष्टितं, यतस् त्वं साधुर् अपि दुःखं प्रापितोऽसीत्य् अत आह---सोऽहं हरेः प्रसादात् तस्य पदवीं माहात्म्यं पश्यन् गत-विस्मयोऽत्र भूतले नान्योपलक्ष्यो गूढः सन् सुखं विचरामि । कथं-भूतस्य ? मर्त्य-विडम्बनेनैश्वर्याच् छादकेन मानुष्यानुकरणेन नृणां दृशश् चित्त-वृत्तीश् चालयतो भ्रामयतः ॥४२॥
word_for_word: tvam sādhuḥ api duḥkham prāpitaḥ asi
you, though virtuous, were made to suffer
seeing the greatness of His path/feet
hidden and not noticed by others
by the imitation of mortality that covers His majesty
causing the eyes and movements of mind of people to wander
entries.literal_english: It is indeed a wonder that, although his misconduct was known, you, who are virtuous, were made to suffer. Therefore, by Hari’s grace, I see the greatness of His path and am free from astonishment. Hidden and unnoticed by others on this earth, I move about happily. Hari’s majesty is covered by an imitation of mortality—by His imitation of human life, He causes people’s eyes and movements of mind to wander.

transliteration: aho svalu vismayo jānato’pi tasyaivaṃ duśceṣṭitaṃ, yatas tvaṃ sādhur api duḥkhaṃ prāpito’sīty ata āha---so’haṃ hareḥ prasādāt tasya padavīṃ māhātmyaṃ paśyan gata-vismayo’tra bhūtale nānyopalakṣyo gūḍhaḥ san sukhaṃ vicarāmi | kathaṃ-bhūtasya ? martya-viḍambanenaiśvaryāc chādakena mānuṣyānukaraṇena nṛṇāṃ dṛśaś citta-vṛttīś cālayato bhrāmayataḥ ||42|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : ahaṃ tu tat-saṅgy api bhagavat-prasādānna tādṛśājñānavān | atas tat-saṅgaṃ tyaktvā tad-vārtā-śravaṇe’pi nirviṇṇaḥ san lokeṣv ātmānaṃ gopayaṃś carāmīty āha so’ham iti | gata-vismayaḥ gata-sandehaḥ | atha vidurasya śrī-kṛṣṇe parama-parāyaṇasyāpi vyavahāra-mātra-dṛṣṭyā śrī-kṛṣṇa-parityāgena yāvaj-jīvaṃ dūra-gamanam idaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇenaiva kāritam iti lakṣyate tac ca dhṛtarāṣṭrādi-vyavahārāveśa-parityājanāya svaika-mātra-veśāya ca paścāt-tāpaṃ sampādayitum iti | ataḥ pūrvaṃ yo vidurābhiprāyo vyākhyātaḥ so’pi tad-icchayaiva jāta iti jñeyam ||42|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : kiṃ ca, mayi tasya droho na mamāpakārako’bhūt, pratyuta paramopakāraka evābhūd ity āha---so’ham iti | martyānāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrādīnāṃ sva-prasādālambhanād viḍambanena vañcanena nṛṇāṃ tat-sadṛśānām anyeṣām api prākṛtānāṃ dṛśor buddhi-vṛttīś cālayato bhramayato hareḥ prasādāt tat-padavīṃ, tasya caraṇa-vinyāsa-vartma caraṇau ca paśyan, bhakta-vatsalasya bhagavataḥ kiyad etad āścaryaṃ ? iti gata-vismayaḥ kvāpy etad-rahasyānudghāṭanād anenopalakṣyaḥ san atra tīrtheṣv eva carāmi | atra duryodhana-niḥsāritasya kheda-samudre nimajjito vidurasya pratyakṣībhūya bhagavatā tasminn eva kāle evaṃ uktaṃ---bho mat-parama-bhakta vidura ! mad-viraham anusmṛtya kim ity evaṃ khidyase? yatra yatra tvaṃ yiyāsasi, tatra tatraiva tīrthe tad-agre calantaṃ tvayā saha kṛta-saṃvādam eva māṃ paśyann eva yāsyasīti bhagavad-varo’numīyate, ata eva duryodhana-vadhānantaram api yudhiṣṭhira-rājya-prāptāv api bhagavad-darśanānanda-nirvṛtenaiva vidureṇa nāyātam, anyathā avaśyam āyāsyataiva | kiṃ ca, mauṣala-līlānte’ntardadhatā bhagavatā vidura-netrād apy antarhitam | ata eva tad-avadhi uddhava-darśana-paryantaṃ vidurasya vaikalyam ||42|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit:
ननु हरेः किम् एवं लीलया, येन स्व-भक्तानां वन-वासादि-क्लेशा भवन्ति, स्वस्य च दौत्ये बन्धनोद्यमादि-पराभवः, तद् वरं तेषाम् अपराधानन्तरम् एव हननं नापराधोपेक्षेत्य् अत आह---नूनं निश्चितं त्रिभिर् मदैर् उत्पथानां उद्वृत्तानां वधाद् धेतोः प्रपन्नानाम् आर्ति-जिहीर्षयेशोऽघ-समय एव हन्तुं समर्थोऽपि कुरूणाम् अघं उपैक्षत । तदानीम् एव तेषां वधे सर्व-दुष्ट-राज-वधो न स्याद् इत्य् आशयेनेत्य् अर्थः ।

> विद्या-मदो धन-मदस् तथैवाभिजनो मदः । >
> एते मदा मदान्धानां त एव हि सतां दमाः ॥ इति त्रयो मदाः > ॥४३॥
word_for_word: ‘Why does Hari act in this way through play?’
so that His devotees undergo the hardships of exile and the like
and He Himself suffers defeat through embassy, attempted imprisonment and the like
tad varam teṣām aparādha-anantaram eva hananam
then it would be better to kill them immediately after their offense
He should not overlook the offense
of those deviating and arrogant through three prides
with the desire to remove the distress of the surrendered
īśaḥ agha-samaya eva hantum samarthaḥ api
although the Lord was able to kill them at the very time of the offense
He overlooked the offense of the Kurus
if they had been killed at that time
the killing of all wicked kings would not have occurred
pride of learning, pride of wealth and pride of birth
these are the prides of the pride-blinded
these very things are restraints for the virtuous
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara raises the objection: why does Hari allow His devotees the hardships of exile while He Himself undergoes defeat through embassy, attempted imprisonment and similar acts? It would seem better to kill the offenders immediately rather than overlook their offense. The answer is that the Lord, desiring to remove the distress of the surrendered, waited to kill the arrogant men who had gone astray through three kinds of pride, although He was capable of killing them at once. If they had been killed then, all the wicked kings would not have been destroyed. The three prides are pride of learning, wealth and birth; these make the arrogant blind, whereas in the virtuous they become restraints.

entries.sanskrit: सर्व-दुर्वृत्त-वधाद्य्-अर्थम् एव भगवतो जन्म-कर्माणि नान्यथेति कैमुत्य-न्यायेनाह---अजस्यापि जन्म, अकर्तुर् अपि कर्माणि, पुंसां ग्रहणाय कर्मसु प्रवृत्तये । अन्यथा न चेद् एव, तर्हि भगवतो जन्मादि-कथा तावद् आस्ताम् । को वान्योऽपि गुणानां परो गुणातीतो देह-योगं कर्म-विस्तारं वाऽर्हतीति ॥४४॥
word_for_word: only for the purpose of killing the wicked and the like
he says by the argument ‘what need is there to say more?’
then let the story of the Lord’s birth and so on stand
kaḥ vā anyaḥ api guṇānām paraḥ
is fit for embodiment or the expansion of activity?
entries.literal_english: Only for the purpose of killing the wicked and the like are the Lord’s births and actions, not otherwise. [The reasoning is a fortiori:] Even the Unborn has a birth; even the non-agent has actions, to attract people and engage them in action. If not otherwise, then let the account of the Lord’s birth and so on stand aside for now. Who else—beyond the guṇas and transcending them—is fit to take on a body or expand action?

transliteration: sarva-durvṛtta-vadhādy-artham eva bhagavato janma-karmāṇi nānyatheti kaimutya-nyāyenāha---ajasyāpi janma, akartur api karmāṇi, puṃsāṃ grahaṇāya karmasu pravṛttaye | anyathā na ced eva, tarhi bhagavato janmādi-kathā tāvad āstām | ko vānyo’pi guṇānāṃ paro guṇātīto deha-yogaṃ karma-vistāraṃ vā’rhatīti ||44|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : ajasya janmety āvirbhāva-mātraṃ tad ity arthaḥ | akartuḥ karmāṇīti svaira-līlā ity arthaḥ | puṃsāṃ sarveṣāṃ grahaṇāya svasmin manasa ākarṣaṇāya | yathoktaṃ pañcame---yal-līlāṃ mṛga-patir ādade’navadyām ādātuṃ sva-jana-manāṃsy udāra-vīrya\[bhā|pu| 5.25.10\] iti | ato deha-yogam iti pitṛtvena svīya-kriyamāṇānāṃ deheṣv āvirbhāva-mātram ity arthaḥ | guṇānāṃ paraḥ kaḥ pārṣadādir api ||44|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : nanu cid-ghanānanda-rūpasya bhagavataḥ kim evaṃ prākṛta-loka-bhadrābhadra-madhya-vartitvena ? satyam | sva-bhakteṣu vātsalyam anyatra sarvatrāpi hitaiṣitvam iti dvāv eva tatra hetuḥ ity āha---ajasya jīvavan māyādhīnatayā janmādi-vikāra-rahitasyāpi janma yoga-māyayā bhakta-premādhīnatayā janmādi-vilāsavattvamutpathānāṃ san-mārga-cchidyam asurāṇāṃ nāśanāya sva-kartṛka-nāśanena teṣāṃ mokṣa-dānāya, akartuḥ nāsya karmaṇi janmādāv ity-ukta-diśā sattvādi-guṇa-nibandhana-kartṛtva-rahitasyāpi karmāṇi cid-ānanda-mayāni govardhanoddharaṇādīni | puṃsāṃ sva-bhaktānāṃ sarvatra svarga-mokṣādi-sukheṣv api viraktānāṃ grahaṇāya āsvādanīyatvena svīkārāya | yad vā, puṃsāṃ mukta-mumukṣu-sāṃsārikāṇāṃ jīvānāṃ grahaṇāya svasminn ākarṣaṇāya nivṛtta-tarṣair upagīyamānād\[bhā|pu| 10.1.4\] ity-ādeḥ | na tv anyathā jīvānāṃ sva-karmādhīnam eva yathā janma karma na tathā ity arthaḥ | karmādhīna-janma-karmavattve dehenāpi tasya sambandhaḥ karmādhīna eva syāt | sa ca deha-yogo guṇātīta-bhakti-siddha-jīvasyāpi nāsti kiṃ punaḥ sākṣāt parameśvarasya tasyety āha---guṇānāṃ paraḥ guṇebhyaḥ pṛthag-bhūtaḥ sann api kaḥ khalu jīvo’pi karma-tantraṃ karmādhīnaṃ deha-yogam arhati, api tu na ko’pi | atra karma-tantraṃ deha-yogaṃ nārhatīty ukte akarma-tantraṃ deha-yogam arhatīty artho labhyate | tasya parameśvarasya tu māyayā sahayogāsambhavāt tad-dehasya cid-ānanda-ghanatvaṃ svata evāyātam ||44|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: तस्माद् एवं-भूताचिन्त्य-माया-विनोदस्य कथां कथयेत्य् आह---तस्य प्रपन्ना येऽस्विल-लोक-पालास् तेषाम् अन्येषां च स्वीयेऽनुशासने स्थितानाम् अर्थाय यदुषु जातस्य । तीर्थं संसार-तारिणी कीर्तिर् यस्येति ॥४५॥
word_for_word: of Him whose play with Māyā is inconceivable and of this kind
of Him to whom all the guardians of the worlds have surrendered
for them and for others also
for the benefit of those situated under His own rule
who was born among the Yadus
whose fame is a sacred ford that carries one across saṃsāra
entries.literal_english: Therefore, tell the story of Him whose play with inconceivable Māyā is of this kind. He was born among the Yadus for the sake of the guardians of all the worlds who have surrendered to Him, and of others situated under His own rule. His fame is a sacred ford that carries one across saṃsāra.

transliteration: tasmād evaṃ-bhūtācintya-māyā-vinodasya kathāṃ kathayety āha---tasya prapannā ye’svila-loka-pālās teṣām anyeṣāṃ ca svīye’nuśāsane sthitānām arthāya yaduṣu jātasya | tīrthaṃ saṃsāra-tāriṇī kīrtir yasyeti ||45|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : hanta hanta sā durvārtā mayā prabhāse śrutaiva tadāpy uttaram adadāne’pi tvayi pratyavayavaṃ yat spṛṣṭaṃ tat khalu vilapitam eva | tasmāj janmādi-līlām eva tad-vismaraṇāya śrotum icchāmīty āha---tasyeti ||45|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : atas tasya cid-ghanānanda-rūpāṇi janma-karmāṇy eva kathayety āśayenāha---tasya prapannā ye’khila-loka-pālās teṣām anyeṣāṃ ca svīye anuśāsane sthitānām arthāya prayojanāya | tīrthaṃ parama-pāvanī saṃsāra-tāriṇī ca kīrtir yasya tasya | sarveṣu tīrtheṣu prāyaḥ kṛta-majjana evāsmi | samprati tvaṃ teṣāṃ sāphalyaṃ upādāya kṛṣṇasya kīrti-tīrthāmṛte māṃ nimajjayeti bhāvaḥ ||45|| iti sārārtha-darśinyāṃ harṣiṇyāṃ bhakta-cetasām | tṛtīye prathamo’dhyāyaḥ saṅgataḥ saṅgataḥ satām ||\|| ——————————————————————————————————————— iti śrīmad-bhāgavate mahā-purāṇe brahma-sūtra-bhāṣye pāramahaṃsyaṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vaiyāsikyāṃ tṛtīya-skandhe viduroddhava-saṃvāde prathamo’dhyāyaḥ | ||3.1|| ——————————————————————————————————————— (3.2)
